rationale: The source defines the Research Knowledge architecture, authority model, identity boundaries, and system constitution for storing and governing research; it is platform infrastructure rather than a market hypothesis, Study, Case, Component, or Formal Edge.

The source is a representability and ontology stress test for the Research Knowledge architecture, checking identity and authority boundaries such as Case versus Company; it validates the platform design rather than researching a market mechanism.

The source defines deterministic cross-record semantic validation, chronology, integrity layers, and repository-wide Research Knowledge consistency rules; these are governance and validation infrastructure, not an independent research identity.

The source defines the read-only adapter boundary for external authorities, including deterministic IDs and point-in-time availability rules while forbidding identity invention or authority mutation; this is integration infrastructure rather than market research.

The source is the Research OS specification itself and explicitly assigns the OS the role of storing, validating, and auditing research while prohibiting it from inventing Edges; it is foundational system infrastructure.

The source defines the append-only point-in-time price data substrate, observation and executability clocks, revision identity, and data-boundary guarantees used by downstream research and evaluation; it is data infrastructure rather than a market hypothesis.

The source governs append-only Recommendation to Outcome to Learning lineage and separates human adoption from automated evaluation while explicitly denying automatic trading or Edge promotion; it is decision and learning governance infrastructure.

The source defines the governed investment-committee decision layer, including jurisdiction, veto, abstention, evidence normalization, and calibration boundaries; it is system-level decision governance rather than a reusable market mechanism or standalone research topic.

The source defines the J-Quants Free PriceProvider adapter, entitlement and licensing boundaries, and point-in-time verification behavior, and explicitly positions J-Quants as verification infrastructure rather than the source of Edge discovery.

The source reviews identity, time, evidence, execution, replay, and decision-governance controls required before expanding active Edges; its findings harden the research foundation and do not constitute an empirical market Study or Edge.
